Sanger High students were exposed to graphic abortion and sexual imagery through a dual-enrollment art course at Reedley College. The school board is now facing intense pressure to review these partnerships.

The Bright Side:
This incident forces a necessary conversation about the boundaries of dual-enrollment programs and parental rights in curriculum selection.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT vs WHO error. The school focuses on the 'what' (academic freedom) while parents focus on the 'who' (the developmental stage of the students).

Social Physics Analysis:
The school used institutional autonomy as a pretext to avoid vetting, while parents projected their concerns onto the board. Transparency would have prevented this friction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The failure to align curriculum with student age creates systemic strain.

The Unavoidable Truth: Institutions often prioritize administrative convenience over individual student needs.
The Unavoidable Lie: Academic freedom justifies exposing minors to graphic content without parental consent.
